html:
SMTO-EXE-0143 — SMTO couldn't find that button or field in the app

GUID: a7070c8b-76d5-5c8c-81cf-b221cac83fb9
Slug: ui-element-not-found
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • SMTO searched the whole app window for the button or field it wanted and didn't find it. It may not be on screen yet or may have a different name. SMTO didn't click or type anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the computer running the Gateway, check that the app shows the screen, tab or dialog where the button or field lives. SMTO only searches what the window currently contains, so a control on another page can't be found.
  2. Tell SMTO the exact wording shown on the button or next to the field, for example 'the Save button in the File menu'. SMTO matches names exactly, so a slightly different word means no match.
  3. If the control appears only after something loads, tell SMTO to wait for it before acting. SMTO can watch for a control to appear instead of searching once too early.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's next step in the task shows it found the button or field.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the app name and the label you can see, to the person who manages that Gateway. Some apps don't share their controls with accessibility tools at all.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A complete scoped accessibility scan of the target window found no element matching the submitted locator.

What this means

  • A complete scoped accessibility scan produced no element matching the submitted locator. Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.

Why this can happen

  • A complete scoped accessibility scan produced no element matching the submitted locator.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the current window, ancestor scope and locator against a fresh bounded snapshot; retain the distinction from an incomplete scan.

How to fix it

  • Take a fresh scoped ui.snapshot on the selected Gateway and compare the element names, roles and automation IDs with the locator. Correct the locator (exact matching is the default; exact=false gives case-insensitive substring matching) or use ui.wait_for until the intended control appears.
  • Inspect the current scoped snapshot and correct the locator or wait for the intended control to appear.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect ui.status and a fresh scoped ui.snapshot on the selected Gateway. Correct the target or prerequisites before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended control is present and uniquely resolves in the supported scope.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
